rationale: Evidence: iteration 10 is the best verified design (374.4). Its oval result is 20 of 20 finishes, mean progress 0.998, mean time 1.88 s, and rms_error 0.014. Its s-bend (progress 0.32) and slalom (progress 0.10) still leave the tape, with about 1 line-loss event per run. Dropping base_speed from 1.3 to 1.2 is the only change that has moved the result, since the kd and kp changes in iterations 6, 8 and 9 left scores unchanged. The held-back track has a different shape, so the robot has to survive bends, not just finish the oval. The failures on s-bend and slalom are tight alternating bends where the robot runs wide and exits the 0.06 m band. Speed is the lever that has shown an effect, so I am taking it further in the same direction. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.2 to 1.1, giving more time to correct at bends. Oval finish time should rise from about 1.88 s to about 2.05 s, still well inside the 3.0 s limit. The time term loses about 2 points and completion should hold. (2) Keep the verified geometry exactly: 8 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016 m, y = 0.06 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg. (3) Keep kp 2.0, ki 0.1 and kd 0.6, which are verified. Expected result: oval completion at or near 1.0, s-bend progress above 0.35, slalom progress above 0.11, and line_loss_events and steering_oscillation at or below iteration 10 levels. Risk: the slower speed may cost finish reliability on the oval. The telemetry should show whether bend progress rises.
